newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Nestle sales rise 17.5 percent in H1.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Nestle sales rise 17.5 percent in H1.

text.p: Nestle SA said first-half sales rose 17.5 percent to 33.5 billion Swiss francs, helped by favourable currency rates and rising volume growth.
"The favourable foreign exchange rates contributed nearly 11 percent to the increase in consolidated sales," the world's biggest food company said in a statement on first-half turnover.
"Real internal growth, not including acquisitions and divestments, stands at 2.7 percent, while it amounted to only 2.2 percent during the first three months of the year," it said.
"Internal growth rates were particularly high in North America and in Eastern Europe, as well as in the Middle East and in Southeast Asian countries," it said.

"Significant progress was realised in pet care products, in the Perrier-Vittel (mineral water) group and in Alcon (pharmaceuticals). Coffee also showed positive volume growth, in spite of the price increases made necessary as a result of the rise in green coffee prices."
It gave no other details on sales or profits.
The 17.5 percent rise was down from the 18.7 percent growth rate in the first quarter, reflecting in part slightly less favourable exchange rates.
The results were published before Swiss share trading began.

"For 1997 as a whole, the Nestle group remains confident that the favourable rate of internal growth will continue. Consolidated sales should therefore also grow, albeit at a slower rate than during the first half of 1997 as a result of the expected foreign exchange evolution," it said.
"As for consolidated net profit, Nestle expects it to evolve in line with consolidated sales."
